name: Anime Edit SFX And Voice Line Spotting
use_when: An anime-style, AMV, game, sports, or action edit needs whooshes, impacts, elemental textures, glitches, risers, or identity voice lines.
A visually polished edit feels flat because motion, impacts, and character moments have no matching sound.
A voice line can identify the character, raise intensity, or set up the clip's emotional beat.
avoid_when: The voice line or SFX source is unlicensed, unclear, or unsafe for the release.
The cue competes with dialogue, narration, or the song's key moment.
The edit already has too many impacts and needs space rather than more sound.

timeline_pattern.pattern: locked_visual_hit -> import_licensed_sfx -> place_whoosh_hit_or_texture -> place_identity_voice_line_if_needed -> trim_fade_tail -> full_mix_review
timeline_pattern.spotting_rule: Spot SFX after the visual timing is locked enough that hits can be placed on real motion frames.
timeline_pattern.event_match_rule: Choose cue families by visible job: clip starts, lightning entrances, glass-break overlays, eye transformations, and character voice moments should not share one generic hit.
timeline_pattern.voice_rule: Place identity voice lines at the beginning of the relevant clip only when they make the moment clearer or more intense.
timeline_pattern.library_rule: Tag reusable SFX by job, such as whoosh, hit, impact, texture, glitch, riser, transition, or character voice.

motion.rule: Each SFX cue should correspond to a visible motion, impact, reveal, transformation, or transition.

sound.rule: Layer cues so they support the music rather than fighting it.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: For hard impacts or transition hits, aim to land within 1-2 frames of the visual peak.
keyframe_values.clip_start_cue: When the cue sells a clip entrance, align it to the first readable frame of the character or effect, not to the nearest music beat by habit.
keyframe_values.voice_line_start: Start short identity voice lines at or just before the clip's opening beat when they are used as an anchor.
keyframe_values.tail_fade: Use short fades on SFX tails so the next clip or voice line is not masked.
keyframe_values.mix_review: Review SFX with the full song and any dialogue restored, not only while soloed.

captions.rule: Caption voice lines only when they are story-critical or hard to understand, and keep them away from the action focus.

color.rule: No direct color rule; audio cues paired with flashes or glow must not hide action readability.

implementation.ffmpeg: Align SFX with adelay/amix, add afade on starts or tails, and track cue frames in an EDL or JSON timeline.
implementation.remotion: Trigger Audio clips from the same frame constants used for visual impacts, transition peaks, and voice-line starts.
implementation.blender: Use timeline audio markers for whoosh, impact, texture, and voice-line placement.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Import files through Sounds > Device > Select from device, place each cue under the matching clip or transition, and adjust timing/tails by preview.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use SFX bins by job, sequence markers at impact frames, clip gain, short fades, and full-mix review before export.

common_mistakes: Using random SFX because they sound intense rather than because they match the clip.
Using one cue family for unrelated events such as lightning, glass break, eye transformation, and voice identity.
Placing voice lines over every clip instead of only identity or impact moments.
Leaving SFX tails to cover the next transition or line.
Ignoring music rights or assuming downloaded SFX are automatically cleared.
Judging SFX while soloed and then burying the song or dialogue in the full mix.
qc: Does every SFX cue have a visible motion, impact, reveal, or character job?
Do cue families match the visible event rather than only the edit's general intensity?
Do hard hits land within the intended sync tolerance?
Do voice lines clarify identity or emotion instead of adding clutter?
Are cue sources licensed, platform-safe, or marked temp-only?
Does the full mix preserve music, dialogue, and SFX clarity without clipping?
